newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds slip, German yield gap to widen more.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds slip, German yield gap to widen more.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped on Thursday and the 10-year bond yield gap with Germany widened and was expected to continue doing so with prices holding levels.

"If the German market rises again after the U.S. February trade figures, we will in all probability not follow suit so the yield gap could widen to 75 points or more but prices should hold more or less," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.06 point from the opening but 0.16 point up from Thursday's close at 109.56, yielding 6.54 percent.

The 2006 benchmark's turnover was just short of one billion crowns while its June future rose 0.21 point to 108.97 with 430 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.03 point to 87.93.
The crown traded at 3.8087 per mark at 1115 gmt, down ever so marginally from 3.8085 at the opening.

The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened two basis points to 74. The Central Bank was active on the market selling an unknown but limited quantity of bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
